title: Continuous adjugate inverse of an everywhere nonsingular finite matrix
statement: Let $F$ be a normed field and $X$ any topological space. Let $n\geq0$ and let $A:X\to M_n(F)$ be continuous for the product topology on finite matrices [def-weil-matrix]. Suppose $\det A(x)\ne0$ for every $x\in X$, with determinant as in [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Define $B(x)=(\det A(x))^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(A(x))$, where the adjugate is the transpose of the cofactor matrix, with empty adjugate the empty matrix. Then $B:X\to M_n(F)$ is continuous and $A(x)B(x)=B(x)A(x)=I_n$ for every $x$. The assertion includes $X=\varnothing$ and $n=0$; it requires neither completeness nor a nontrivial norm.
